transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Let's get started with the recovery huddle for the P-4 palletizer situation. We've got an urgent outbound order at the end of the week, so we need to work through maintenance status, shipment staging, and energy-isolation controls before we can execute anything. I need each of you to give me your current findings so I can make a decision on the recovery method. Let's start with maintenance — what's the status on P-4?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Here's what I found during my inspection this morning. P-4 has a damaged gearbox bearing. The good news is the replacement seal is stocked on site, so we have what we need. The repair will take exactly 6 hours and requires exactly 6 lockout points. I completed the inspection already, but I should note the formal maintenance report is still awaiting my supervisor's signoff, so I'm giving you my current findings verbally for now.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a staging capacity issue. I've confirmed from the carrier booking and warehouse count that exactly 800 pallets must be staged by Friday at 15:00. The manual palletizing station can only complete 240 pallets per shift, so with two shifts remaining it cannot meet this shipment requirement. I haven't entered the confirmed count into the recovery board yet, but I wanted everyone aware now so we can factor this into the recovery decision.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share a critical safety finding before we go any further. My safety review confirmed that P-4's repair requires an authorized electrician to verify zero energy at all six lockout points and record that verification before any maintenance starts. This requirement is not yet attached to the work order because the incident review is still open, but it must be documented in the recovery plan and followed before anyone begins work on P-4.
transcript.speaker: A4
